customManagers.description: Cubeship template.yaml: image + tag pairs under apps/

packageRules.description: An upstream release changes what the template deploys, so it has to cut a new template version. 'chore' is invisible to release-please and would strand the update on main.
An upstream patch is a fix, not a feature: same shape, corrected behaviour.
Majors are migrations, not tag changes — flag them loudly.
CI tooling does not change what users deploy, so it stays out of the changelog and cuts no release.

ClickHouse follows Plausible, not the newest release. Plausible's own compose.yml pins clickhouse-server 24.12-alpine, and Plausible talks to it with its own queries and schema. Taking a ClickHouse the app does not test would break the template for whoever installs it, and nothing here would catch that. Patches inside 24.12 still come through; moving to 25.x or 26.x is a decision that follows an upstream bump.
